description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between “o_pop frequency (x10^4)” on the x-axis and “Accuracy” on the y-axis, comparing two metrics: “Initial Accuracy” (green line with square markers and error bars) and “Final Accuracy” (blue dashed line with circular markers and error bars). The x-axis spans from 1 to 19 in increments of 2, representing o_pop frequency scaled by 10^4. The y-axis ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 in increments of 0.2, indicating accuracy as a proportion. The green “Initial Accuracy” line begins at approximately 0.35 at x=1, rises to a peak of ~0.5 at x=5, dips to ~0.3 at x=7, rises again to ~0.5 at x=13, then declines to ~0.35 at x=17 before slightly increasing to ~0.4 at x=19. The blue “Final Accuracy” line starts at ~0.65 at x=1, increases to ~0.8 at x=5, dips to ~0.7 at x=7, peaks at ~0.9 at x=9, drops to ~0.7 at x=11, rises to ~0.9 at x=15, dips to ~0.8 at x=17, and ends at ~0.9 at x=19. Both lines exhibit fluctuations across the x-axis, with Final Accuracy consistently higher than Initial Accuracy at all points, and both showing error bars that indicate variability in measurements.
